doc_text:
as of april 2, california had a relatively low number of coronavirus cases per capita, compared to new york, new jersey, and louisiana.  california health officials and politicians, don't pat yourself on the back just yet.  just check the number of covid-19 tests processed: new york 239,000 and california 33,000.  

as of march 31, one of california's major commercial lab testers of covid-19, quest diagnostics, had 115,000 covid-19 test results pending in 12 labs across the country.   this is due partly to a shortage of trained technicians to run the lab test machines, and a shortage of the testing reagents, many of which imported from china and other countries.  california itself has 59,500 covid-19 test results pending, with test results taking up to 10 days.  the state with the second most reported pending results is florida with 77,000 tests processed and 1,280 covid-19 test results pending. 

trump got his second covid-19 test result in 15 minutes.  much more essential people like emergency room doctors, er nurses, critical care nurses, anesthesiologists, nurse anesthetists, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, respiratory therapists, respiratory therapist technicians, intensive care technicians, emergency medical technicians, medical workers, health care workers, paramedics, medical first responders, police, and firefighters have been quarantined at home, away from work, for 10-12 days before finding out their covid-19 result were negative!  

worse yet, such an essential worker, negative at the time of testing, could be infected within the 10 day test result waiting period, receive their negative result from 10 days earlier, show no symptoms, and then go back to work infecting their professional work colleagues in addition to the patients they contact.

patient stays longer in hospitals awaiting covid-19 test results of up to 10 days.  subsequent heavier demands and usage of hospital staffing, hospital supplies, hospital bedding availability, and personal protective equipment, all of which already in short supply.    

an out patient may have flown on a full airplane, ridden on a bus, or gone to overcrowded stores like costco or walmart, infecting countless others, by the time a positive result is obtained 10 days later.     

the state is looking for other private labs to run covid-19 tests.  abbott labs just rolled out a covid-19 test that can get results in 5-13 minutes, manufacturing up to 50,000 test cartridges a day.  the white house gets them, but gives each state only 15 machines and 100 cartridges of these test kits.  so wyoming with 579,000 people gets the same number of test kits as california with 39,900,000 people.  we will have to continue to rely on getting results from quest diagnostics, with results taking  up to 10 days.  

california's april 3 count of 11290 coronavirus cases may be that of 10 days earlier-march 24, and is completely misleading.  the actual number of positive covid-19 results as of april 3 may be triple that, but won't be reported until 10 days from now, on april 13.

on the positive side: quest diagnostics backlog of 115,000 pending covid-19 test results on march 31 is an improvement of the 160,000 pending covid-19 test results on march 25.

april 21 update: new york has processed 669,982 tests or 34,151 per million residents, ranking 1st of the 50 states.  california has processed 300,100 tests or 7,666 per million residents, ranking 46th of the 50 states. 

on april 19 a panel of experts published a report saying that to begin to open up the country, 5 million tests would have to be processed daily.  to bring the economy up to full speed, 30 million tests would have to be processed daily.  not going to happen relying on private labs like quest diagnostics.

i have been a patient of dr. hoelchers' for several years and have seen several concerning patterns within his practice.

this dr. does not respect the time of his customers (patients). i went in for my annual checkup having labs done two weeks prior and was told during my appointment that i needed to schedule another appointment to review my lab work. i would have appreciated a phone call stating that my labs were not available and that i would need to reschedule my appointment if it was a requirement that my labs were reviewed with me in person so that i could schedule another appointment. this no doubt could have been uploaded to my patient portal and discussed with me over the phone, saving me from paying for another office visit and the time that it takes out of my busy schedule to go to another appointment. nevertheless as requested i scheduled another appointment.

on the date of the subsequent appointment i was 12 minutes late due to being required to fill out paperwork at my job (dod) before i left for the day due to contingency situations with covid 19. i was then told that it was their policy that a $45 no show fee is charged if the customer is more than 10 minutes late for their appointment and there was no way that they could remove the charge. i stated that i would gladly wait for my appointment that same day because all we were doing was going over labwork. i was then told that i needed to either reschedule or i could get a telemedicine appointment the next day where i will no doubt be charged for another appointment and an additional fee for telemedicine.

in my most recent appointment, i was also informed that i was being charged for something over a year later that was covered under my insurance plan.

additionally, you do not see the dr. at all you see a pa where previously i was seeing dr. hoelscher directly. the pa is nice, thorough, and takes the time to answer any questions that you have, but  i may not be receiving the level of care that i previously had been receiving. 

furthermore, the front office staff have no empathy for their customers at all and act like mindless automata. all forms are printed and as a blind person, i have requested numerous times that my forms be sent in an accessible format or to be filled out prior to the appointment via the patient portal so that i can fill them out myself. why in 2020 are they still using a paper questionnaire when all of this information is then typed into a computer later on? i have informed the staff about how to make these forms accessible and more convenient for their patients time and time again, but i keep getting told that "there is no way for us to accomplish that." this has the alternative benefit of minimizing the spread of microorganisms, etc. i am sure that other offices have no doubt figured it out.

doc_text:
i have a number of autoimmune disorders and take a very heavy-duty immunosuppressant plus another daily, weaker med that does the same thing. so when i get sick, i get significantly sicker than your average patient. i went to the minute clinic last week with a severely swollen and sore throat, low-grade fever, evidence of infection in my sinuses, cough and inflamed lymph nodes. saw a nurse practitioner who took a strep culture and gave me lidocaine for the throat. i have no issue with her treatment, as i feel waiting for results was reasonable.

however, the next day (which is now five days after i initially got sick), i was significantly worse. at this point, my tonsils were swollen so badly, i was worried about it affecting my breathing and i called to see if she could prescribe something while we waited for the strep test. it was a different np this day and she refused to even speak with me and, as it was relayed to me, was "annoyed" i hadn't gone through "proper channels" to ask my question. 

later that day, the strep culture came back negative. the nurse still refused to speak with me, told me through her lpn that it was a virus that just needed to "run its course" and wouldn't listen when i tried to explain that my immune system isn't going to be able to fight it without some medical intervention.

the following day, now day 6, i was still worse, but now i was having chest pain and difficulty breathing. at this point, i went to urgent care and saw an actual doctor who immediately recognized i needed help. he diagnosed me with strep (and told me that a huge percentage of strep cultures give a false negative because they aren't collected properly) that was rapidly developing into pneumonia, plus a bad case of pink eye. 

it's been almost a week now that i've been on antibiotics, steroids and eye drops and i'm slowly recovering. a lot of this could have been avoided, had the provider at cvs actually listened to me and taken my illness seriously. i understand a viral infection won't respond to antibiotics, but the nurse didn't even offer a steroid. she didn't show any care or concern at all. i definitely won't be going back to any minute clinic, as i felt the level of care was very poor.

i wanted to share my experience so that you can consider whether or not you want to go visit this office or go to another or just be careful when you go. i visited and the staff scratched up my existing glasses and refused to take responsibility for it.  

in earlier march, my eyes were bothering me and after going through a lot of reviews on the doctors and facilities, i made an appointment to see dr. tang on friday, march 6th since it was near my work place. i only had computer glasses from my last doctor so they asked me to bring those glasses with me. when i arrived, after signing in, andres who was in the front asked for my glasses to test my prescription with a machine that brings lenses down like a microscope to my glasses lenses. after a bit, i got it back and then got called in to met with the technician and then dr. tang. 

when i got in, dr. tang asked to look at my glasses so i gave it to him and told him that the front desk tested for the prescription. he looked at it quickly, made a face and then returned it to me. after my examination, since he was not able to identify any issues, dr. tang recommended that i get new glasses with a slightly lower prescription (+0.75 instead of +1.0 that i had) and blue light filter which would help with the strain on my eyes from the computer. i went outside and andres helped me pick out some frames and lens. i don't have much of a preference so picking out the frame and everything did not take long. i paid $200+ for the frames and the lenses to be ordered. since my eyes were dilated, i didn't go back to work after and did not touch my glasses. 

on monday march 9th , when i returned to work, i realized that there were giant circular scratches in the middle of both of my lenses to the point it fully blocks the point of vision. i called the office and told andres about it and he said he would help me with that when i go pick up my new glasses. when my glasses were finally ready for pick up on monday march 16th, they notified me around 2pm so i left work early to go get them since they were closing at 5pm. when i arrived, i got the glasses fitted so it only took a few minutes. 

after that, andres asked to see my old glasses and said unfortunately, they can't prove that the scratched were made by them. he said he look at the machine after i called but can't prove anything. the scratches are literally circular scratches in the middle of the lenses that matches where the the equipment touched my lenses.i tried to reason with him and say how else would i have gotten that. he said the only courtesy they can do was to charge me $25 to replace the lenses. i could have asked them to put it on the machine and see if the scratches matches their machine but didn't seem like it was worth it and i didn't feel like arguing so i asked how long it would take, he said he couldn't do it today and told me to leave it with him. the girl next to him eventually chimmed in and said it would be a leap of faith at this point to leave it with them since they don't know what would happen with covid19 so she recommends me to not leave it. 

i decided against leaving it since i'd rather have my $400+ frames and get it fixed elsewhere just in case they close. on march 17th, i received an email from them saying they are temporarily closed as of 5pm that day so good thing i didn't leave it with them. i didn't think i would need to immediate check my glasses after it was checked since i assume they knew what they are doing but i learned my lesson there. i didn't initially know why the doctor made a face when he saw my glasses in the examination room. now thinking back, i assumed it was because he saw the scratches and didn't want to say anything, but i wouldn't know for sure.  

dr. tang was nice and the clinic staff were nice overall but putting giant scratches on my glasses and then refusing to take responsibility especially since i also purchased glasses from them was really disappointing. honestly, unless you have very complicated issues with your eyes, the whole process and experience is routine so it's standard in most places. i switched to a new place because the my previous location is so out of the way since i changed jobs. i've had my glasses for more than 4 years and never had a scratch on them until then since i only wear it occasionally when i am at work and i have ocd. i wrap the glasses back each time with the dust cloth before putting it back into the hard case. i still wanted to keep the old ones as spare since i paid $400+ for the frames when i got it and the prescription was not significantly different. 

i wanted to share this experience so that you are aware and can decide whether or not to go. if you do, be cautious of the handling of your glasses if you have.

shalin supported my husband and i throughout the pregnancy and birth of our first child as our doula, evidence based birth childbirth educator, and lactation educator. 

hiring shalin was one of the best decisions we made in preparation for welcoming our baby. as our doula, her impartial and unwavering support guided us through decision making during our pregnancy and helped us to advocate for the prenatal care and birth preferences we desired. shalin's evidence based birth course equipped us with the knowledge and tools needed for a variety of birth experiences. this left my husband and i feeling more prepared in our roles both as the birthing person and support person leading up to the birth of our baby. lastly, shalin's one-on-one prenatal lactation course helped me to feel much more confident about breastfeeding for the first time knowing that i could trouble shoot common challenges and that i was equipped with the knowledge and resources needed for differing eventualities.

about a month before our estimated due date the covid 19 pandemic hit, causing our hospital to restrict visitors and not allow doulas in the birthing space. shalin calmly and proactively navigated this stressful situation, creating a library of online resource videos and offering virtual support for families in labor once they reached the hospital. she helped us to reformulate our plan for labor and birth to adapt to this less than ideal situation - helping us to regain a sense of control and support and reduce anxiety. 

on our baby's birthday shalin supported us in-person as we labored at home and then seamlessly transitioned to supporting us virtually via zoom and text once we moved to the hospital. her support throughout our pregnancy and birth played a huge role in helping us to achieve the positive and empowering birth experience we had envisioned.
